ci.description: update search index and block tags [skip ci]

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: take the landing label off when a pull request's base changes
ci.body:
The landing label records guards that ran against the branch a pull request
targets. Editing the base sends an edited event, which the Trusted Weavers
workflow does not handle, and its branch filter would skip a retarget away
from main in any case, so the label and the guards comment stayed.

A new workflow, Landing follows the base, starts on every edit of a pull
request into any branch and runs its job only when the base changed. It takes
the label off a pull request that carried it when the base changed and says
in the guards comment which base the guards ran against. It checks out no
code and has no concurrency group, so a later title edit cannot cancel it.

The Trusted Weavers approval and label steps act only while the pull request
still targets the base the checks ran against, and the label step reads the
pull request again once the label and its comment are on, taking the label
back off when the head or the base moved meanwhile.

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the Weaver workflow finds its guards comment by its own author and the leading marker
ci.body:
The three lookups took the first bot comment that contained the marker
anywhere, so a review bot quoting the marker made the workflow try to edit
that bot's comment and fail. They now take github-actions[bot]'s comment
that starts with the marker, which is the one the workflow writes.

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: keep the Weaver workflow's write token in the jobs that write, and trust the base branch's list
ci.body:
The jobs that write labels and comments (clear-landing, approve-and-label,
report-failed-checks, notify-non-weaver) ask for issues and pull-requests
write themselves; the workflow default is read-only. validate-content
installs and runs the pull request's code with a read-only token, and its
checkout keeps no token on disk. The trust check reads .github/WEAVERS.txt
from the base branch, so a pull request that adds its own author counts as
trusted only once it is merged.

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the landing label stays only on a head whose guards passed
ci.body:
Trusted Weavers: runs for one pull request go one at a time, a newer
push cancelling the older run. A push or a reopen takes the label off
before the checks run again, and the guards comment says the label is
off; a label added as the pull request was opened stays. The approval
and the label go only on the commit the run validated, the approval
pinned to it. A head whose checks fail loses the label and the guards
comment says the checks failed; a failed run for an older head leaves
the newer head alone.

In all three flows the label comes off again when its guards comment
cannot be posted. The re-catalog script leaves the label off when the
indexer skipped a file, since that file is missing from the index, and
its PR body counts the skipped files.

The docs export AUTO_CATALOG_LAND in the shell examples and describe
the label's new rules.

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: label pull requests landing where they were merged automatically
ci.body:
The inbox categorizer merged a move at 70 percent confidence or more,
the trusted Weaver workflow merged a validated pull request through the
REST API, and the re-catalog script merged its pull request five
seconds after opening it when asked to. A pull request lands only after
its reviews and comments are read, fixed or answered and its threads
resolved, so each of them keeps its guards, adds the landing label
(created on first use) and posts one comment naming the guards that
passed; a maintainer lands the pull request after that pass.

The Weaver workflow keeps one comment per pull request, takes the label
off when a later push fails the checks, and drops contents: write,
which only the merge needed. The script takes --land and
AUTO_CATALOG_LAND, with --auto-merge and AUTO_CATALOG_MERGE kept as
older names for the same setting.

The test also parses the changed workflows (the YAML, every run block
with bash -n, every github-script body compiled as the action wraps
it) and the script, since GitHub reports a broken workflow file only
when an event would start it.

test.author: jddunn
test.description: the landing label comes off when a pull request's base changes
test.body:
A pull request labelled landing keeps the label when its author moves its
base, though the guards ran against the old base. The tests run a new
workflow's github-script step on an edit that changed the base: it takes the
label off and says so in the guards comment, leaves a pull request without
the label alone, and starts on any base, so a retarget away from main counts.

The Trusted Weavers label and approval steps must also leave a pull request
alone once it targets another base, and take the label back off when the head
or the base moves while the label goes on.

test.author: jddunn
test.description: the Weaver workflow edits only its own guards comment
test.body:
A review bot quoted the guards marker inside its own issue comment on the
pull request that added this flow. The lookup takes the first bot comment
containing the marker, so the update would go to that bot's comment, which
the workflow token cannot edit (403), and no run could label the pull
request. The stand-in for the GitHub API now refuses edits to another
author's comment, and three cases put a quoting comment first.

test.author: jddunn
test.description: the Weaver workflow writes only where it must and trusts the base branch's list
test.body:
The jobs that add labels and comments should hold the write token; the job
that installs and runs the pull request's code should get a read-only token
and keep none in its checkout. The trusted list should come from the base
branch, so a pull request cannot add its own author.

test.author: jddunn
test.description: run the landing flows' own code, and scan nested folders
test.body:
The Trusted Weavers workflow's github-script steps now run against a
stand-in for the GitHub API: a push or a reopen takes the landing label
off before the checks run again, a label added as the pull request is
opened stays, the label and the approval go only on the commit the run
validated, a failed guards comment takes the label off again, and a
failed check takes it off its own head and says so in the comment. The
workflow runs one at a time per pull request.

The inbox workflow's results step and the re-catalog script run in a
scratch repository with stand-ins for gh, curl and npm on the PATH: both
label and comment when their guards pass, take the label off again when
the comment cannot be posted, and never merge; the re-catalog script
leaves the label off when the indexer skipped a file.

The merge-call scan walks nested folders under .github, scripts and lib,
and the github-script compile check no longer counts the steps.

test.author: jddunn
test.description: nothing here merges a pull request by itself
test.body:
Pull requests land only after their reviews and comments are read,
answered and resolved. The test scans every workflow and script for a
merge call (gh pr merge, the REST merge endpoint, Octokit pulls.merge,
the GraphQL auto-merge mutation, a merge action) and checks that the
three flows that would merge keep their guards, add the landing label
and post a comment.

It fails on master: the inbox categorizer merges at 70 percent
confidence, the trusted Weaver workflow merges after validation, and
the re-catalog script merges when asked to.

docs.author: jddunn
docs.description: pull requests land after the comment pass, under the landing label
docs.body:
The README, the quick start, the development and re-catalog guides, the
contributor guide, the workflows page and the architecture overview
described automatic merges. They describe the landing label, the guards
behind it and the review pass before a merge, and give
AUTO_CATALOG_LAND as the re-catalog script's own setting: no workflow
reads it, so it is not listed as a repository secret.

The overview keeps its line count, so the block line numbers in its
frontmatter hold; the renamed heading's block id and text follow it.

chore.author: jddunn
chore.description: bump @framers/* deps to latest published versions

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the bump refreshes package-lock.json with npm install --package-lock-only and commits it, so npm ci agrees with the bumped package.json

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the bump commits package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, the manifests this repository tracks
ci.body:
create-pull-request stages its add-paths with one git add -- <add-paths>, and
git stages nothing when one path matches no file. This repository tracks no
package.json below its root and no .gitmodules, and a plain **/package.json
does not match the root package.json, so the dispatched run 39396254503 moved
@framers/sql-storage-adapter in package.json, refreshed pnpm-lock.yaml, and
stopped at "fatal: pathspec '**/package.json' did not match any files" with
nothing committed and no pull request opened.

add-paths now names package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml. Test Suite run
39460841498 on c578ec8 failed the new case with the same git error.

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the bump's landing label is decided from its guards' runs on every event, listed by workflow file and followed through re-runs, and read again after each write with no concurrency group to cancel runs

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the bump labels nothing; a workflow that follows its Test Suite and rename-guard runs labels its pull request landing once both pass on its head, and keeps the label off a head they have not passed

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: open the bump pull request with FRAMERS_BUMP_TOKEN so its Test Suite and rename-guard jobs run
ci.body:
A pull request a workflow opens or pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN gets its
pull_request runs in an approval-required state with no job. The bump now
pushes its branch and opens its pull request with FRAMERS_BUMP_TOKEN, the
framerslab organization secret shared with this repository, and its own
GITHUB_TOKEN only reads.

A first step fails the run with an error annotation when the secret is
empty. The checkout takes master, so a dispatch from any branch bumps master.
The lockfile refresh runs with --ignore-scripts, and pnpm/action-setup and
create-pull-request are pinned to the commits v6 and v7 point at (v6.0.10 and
v7.0.11). The pull request carries the landing label.

WORKFLOWS.md and the README describe the bump and the secret, and the Test
Suite entry names its real triggers.

test.description: the bump commits every manifest it changes, and each path in its add-paths matches a file here
test.body:
create-pull-request commits with git add -- <add-paths>, and git refuses the
whole add when one pathspec matches no file. The dispatched run 39396254503
changed package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, then logged "fatal: pathspec
'**/package.json' did not match any files" and stopped with nothing
committed: this repository tracks no .gitmodules and no package.json below
its root, and a plain pathspec needs the slash before package.json, so
**/package.json misses the root manifest too.

The new case makes the action's commit in a scratch repository holding this
repository's tracked files, after changing every package.json and
pnpm-lock.yaml, and expects all of them in the commit.

ci.description: github-script moves to v9.0.0, create-pull-request to v8.1.1 and repository-dispatch to v4.0.1, the releases that run on Node.js 24, each pinned to its release's commit with the release named beside it; CodeRabbit skips the index pull request by its title and reviews none of the index files

ci.description: update search index and block tags

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the changelog and the enhanced block tags reach master through pull requests opened with FRAMERS_BUMP_TOKEN, the activity script's merged pull requests query declares only the variables it uses, and the landing label follows ci/changelog and ci/ai-enhance-blocks
ci.body:
changelog.yml runs once a week, Monday 00:00 UTC, instead of daily. One step picks the first day, seven days ago or the day a manual run names, and hands it to both history scripts. The job takes the monthly files of an open changelog pull request before the scripts append, installs nothing, and opens or updates one pull request into master from ci/changelog with create-pull-request at the commit the bump pins; its GITHUB_TOKEN only reads, and no step pushes to master.

fetch-issue-activity.js drops $since from the merged pull requests query. The pullRequests connection takes no date argument, and GitHub refused the query that declared it ("Variable $since is declared by anonymous query but not used", run 34420881812); the date stays applied to mergedAt in the script. The created issues are kept only when created on or after the first day, since the issues filter's since is the update time.

ai-enhance-blocks.yml runs the enhancement in a job whose GITHUB_TOKEN only reads and whose checkout keeps no token, and archives the strands it changed as a patch. On a manual run, a second job opens or updates one pull request into master from ci/ai-enhance-blocks. On a labelled pull request, a second job commits the patch onto the pull request's branch as a fast-forward and pushes it with FRAMERS_BUMP_TOKEN, and no commit message carries a skip marker, so Test Suite and rename-guard run on the new head. The jobs that hold the token run none of the repository's code. The run's inputs reach the script as arguments.

landing-follows-the-bump-checks.yml follows ci/changelog and ci/ai-enhance-blocks beside the bump's and the index's branches.

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the index publish job checks out master's head, so its pull request carries the index alone and merges without a conflict after master took an earlier index pull request; its ordering step reads the run's commit by its id, and a comparison that cannot be made fails the step instead of skipping the publish

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: the index publish job opens one pull request into master from ci/codex-index with FRAMERS_BUMP_TOKEN instead of pushing the index to master, which master's required checks refuse; it publishes from master only, one run at a time, leaves the pull request to the run of a later change to the index's inputs, and archives and downloads with upload-artifact v7 and download-artifact v8; the landing label follows that pull request's Test Suite and rename-guard as it follows the bump's

ci.author: jddunn
ci.description: Update Badges runs on master and publishes shields.io endpoint files on a badges branch, never a commit to master
ci.body:
The job ran only when github.ref was refs/heads/main, a branch this repository does not have, so it was skipped on every master run and the README kept SVG files committed to master in December 2025.

The Unit Tests job now writes one endpoint file per badge from its own run (scripts/badges/write-badge-json.js): tests counted from the coverage run's Vitest JSON report, line coverage from coverage-summary.json, the version from package.json, the licence from LICENSE. On a push to master, after the four test jobs pass, Update Badges replaces the badges branch with them, a parentless commit pushed with --force-with-lease on the head it read (scripts/badges/publish-badges-branch.sh), and purges jsDelivr's copies. It is the only job with contents: write. The README reads the files through jsDelivr, since shields.io refuses github.com addresses.

The SVG generator, its npm scripts and its committed output go, and so does the Codecov upload, which every run refused for want of a token.

commits.body:
changelog.yml runs once a week, Monday 00:00 UTC, instead of daily. One step picks the first day, seven days ago or the day a manual run names, and hands it to both history scripts. The job takes the monthly files of an open changelog pull request before the scripts append, installs nothing, and opens or updates one pull request into master from ci/changelog with create-pull-request at the commit the bump pins; its GITHUB_TOKEN only reads, and no step pushes to master.

fetch-issue-activity.js drops $since from the merged pull requests query. The pullRequests connection takes no date argument, and GitHub refused the query that declared it ("Variable $since is declared by anonymous query but not used", run 34420881812); the date stays applied to mergedAt in the script. The created issues are kept only when created on or after the first day, since the issues filter's since is the update time.

ai-enhance-blocks.yml runs the enhancement in a job whose GITHUB_TOKEN only reads and whose checkout keeps no token, and archives the strands it changed as a patch. On a manual run, a second job opens or updates one pull request into master from ci/ai-enhance-blocks. On a labelled pull request, a second job commits the patch onto the pull request's branch as a fast-forward and pushes it with FRAMERS_BUMP_TOKEN, and no commit message carries a skip marker, so Test Suite and rename-guard run on the new head. The jobs that hold the token run none of the repository's code. The run's inputs reach the script as arguments.

landing-follows-the-bump-checks.yml follows ci/changelog and ci/ai-enhance-blocks beside the bump's and the index's branches.

  --validate; its header, the workflows doc and the guides say so, and point to npm run index -- --validate and the

ci.description: workflows name master alone; the four that ran only for main and the no-op pages workflow are removed
ci.body:
auto-merge-weavers.yml, ai-enhance-pr.yml and async-processing.yml ran only for pull requests into or pushes to main,
and build-index.yml only on a push to it. This repository has no main branch, so no event started them.

- ai-enhance-pr.yml: removed. On master it would call a paid model through scripts/ai-enhance.js on every pull request
  not labelled skip-ai, and its auto-enhance step pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN, which starts no check on the new head.
  ai-enhance-blocks.yml enhances on request, and scripts/ai-enhance.js stays as npm run ai-enhance.
- async-processing.yml: removed. Its publish job pushed a job's commit to the protected branch, its dispatch went to
  framersai/frame.dev, now framerslab/frame.dev, where no workflow listens for repository_dispatch, its validation
  could not fail, and auto-index.yml builds the index. peter-evans/repository-dispatch leaves the pinned list.
- auto-merge-weavers.yml and .github/WEAVERS.txt: removed. A pull request from a fork gets no secrets and a read-only
  token, so the workflow could neither approve nor label one, and on master it would act on every pull request, all of
  them by the one name the list holds, the maintainer's.
- build-index.yml: removed. It force-pushed an index branch nothing reads; auto-index.yml brings the index to master
  through a pull request.
- pages.yml: removed. It echoed one line on every push.
- test.yml: its push and pull request filters name master alone.
- scripts/retrigger-full-catalog.sh opens its pull request into master and checks master out at the end.

The guides and the wiki's architecture thread describe the workflows that remain, and the Trusted Weavers tests go
with the workflow.

docs.description: no workflow calls a model on a pull request unless someone labels it ai-enhance
docs.body:
The README, the quick start, the development guide, the re-catalog guide and the contributor guide said no workflow
calls a model on a pull request, beside the ai-enhance label that starts the block enhancement on one.

test.author: jddunn
test.description: every pull request workflow but the base-change follower starts only for pull requests into master
test.body:
A pull_request trigger with no branch filter starts for a pull request into any branch, so the test now requires
branches: [master] on each one. ai-enhance-blocks.yml (labelled pull requests) and rename-guard.yml have none, so it
fails on this commit. landing-follows-the-base.yml keeps none on purpose: a pull request moved off master carries its
new base in the event, and a master filter would miss the move it exists to see.

test.author: jddunn
test.description: workflows name master or a pull request branch a workflow opens, and the re-catalog script opens its pull request into master
test.body:
tests/workflow-branches.test.js reads every workflow's branch filters, checkout refs, pull request bases and the branch
names in its run steps and scripts, and fails on any branch other than master and the four pull request branches the
workflows open. Six workflows name main, which this repository does not have, and build-index.yml pushes an index
branch, so the test fails on this commit.

The re-catalog script's tests now run in a scratch repository whose branch is master and check the pull request's base;
the script opens its pull request into main and checks main out at the end, so they fail on this commit too.

commits.author: jddunn
commits.description: the labelled block enhancement and rename-guard start only for pull requests into master, and the docs name what calls a model and what the index build leaves alone
commits.body:
- ai-enhance-blocks.yml and rename-guard.yml filter their pull_request triggers to master, so labelling a pull request
  into another branch no longer starts the paid enhancement.
- The inbox categorizer asks a model first for each note pushed under weaves/inbox/ when a model key is set, with no
  cost cap; the README, the quick start and the development guide say so instead of saying a model runs only when
  someone starts one.
- auto-index.yml archives the tracked codex-blocks.json without rebuilding it, and its indexer runs without
  --validate; its header, the workflows doc and the guides say so, and point to npm run index -- --validate and the
  re-catalog script for a run that stops on validation errors.
